Senses.PreferredTarget: the true eye for discerning the teaching
AlternateTargets: the true eye of the teaching
the eye of the true teaching
Senses.Explanation: The true eye for discerning the teaching: an eye-like capacity that the records say a person can possess, lack, brighten, open, or blind. ‘True or correct’ (正) qualifies ‘teaching’ (法) and ‘eye’ (眼), while the converging predicates show that this is not an ordinary anatomical eye. There are 891 standalone occurrences in 234 allowlisted texts after excluding the longer compound ‘treasury of the true eye of the teaching’ (正法眼藏). Touzi Datong says it is better to possess this eye. Linquan Conglun says that someone without it misses at every turn and that someone who possesses it will verify the nirvana-mind; his preface to Linji Yixuan's record also says Linji illuminated the nirvana-mind by means of it. Deshan Huichu speaks of blinding it, and Meixi Fudu asks whether the assembly's eye is bright. The term is also put directly into public questions whose concrete replies are recorded rather than harmonized. An unnamed monk asks Mupingshan Shandao, ‘What is the true eye for discerning the teaching?’ and receives ‘the hole in a staff’ (拄杖孔). In the Ying'an–Mi'an case, Ying'an Tanhua asks the same question and Mi'an Xianjie immediately answers, ‘a broken sand-pot’ (破沙盆). Its Chan deployment is thus a named faculty of discernment publicly claimed, denied, endangered, and tested, without the dictionary deciding which one of those case answers finally defines it.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide standalone sense. Every curated occurrence uses the standalone expression without the following graph for ‘treasury.’ The longer compound has its own entry and is related as a treasury named with this eye. Possession, absence, brightness, opening, blinding, and divergent public answers are predicates or deployments of the same faculty, not separate lexical things.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), in Touzi Datong's instruction on questioning. Touzi returns a message saying that it would be better to possess the true eye for discerning the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 非具正法眼者頭頭蹉過
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linquan Conglun's Empty Hall Collection of Danxia Chun's Verses on Old Cases (林泉老人評唱丹霞淳禪師頌古虗堂集), in Linquan's commentary on case twenty-six. Linquan says that anyone without the true eye for discerning the teaching misses at every turn and conflicts with every matter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若具正法眼，必證涅槃心
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linquan Conglun's Empty Hall Collection of Danxia Chun's Verses on Old Cases (林泉老人評唱丹霞淳禪師頌古虗堂集), in Linquan's commentary on case eighty-one. Linquan says that someone who possesses the true eye for discerning the teaching will verify the nirvana-mind.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄), signed preface by Linquan Conglun. Linquan Conglun is the exact preface author who says that Linji made clear the nirvana mind with the true teaching eye; Linji Yixuan is the person praised, not the speaker of this prefatory clause.

The Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), in Deshan Huichu's section. Deshan says that gathering to raise the matter blinds the true eye for discerning the teaching, then continues his hall address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 菴問：如何是正法眼？師遽答曰：破沙盆。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in Mi'an Xianjie's biography. Ying'an Tanhua asks, ‘What is the true eye for discerning the teaching?’ and Mi'an immediately answers, ‘a broken sand-pot.’ Ying'an is the exact headword-bearing questioner; Mi'an is the respondent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是正法眼。師曰。拄杖孔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Meeting at the Source (五燈會元), in Mupingshan Shandao's section, records an unnamed monk asking, ‘What is the true eye for discerning the teaching?’ Mupingshan answers, ‘the hole in a staff.’ The monk is the exact headword-bearing speaker; Mupingshan is the respondent.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: Unnamed monk asking Mupingshan Shandao about the true teaching-eye
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The unnamed monk is the exact headword-bearing speaker asking Mupingshan Shandao about the true teaching-eye.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然，未審諸人正法眼明否？若也明得，始知妙道目前觀，真宗耳底透。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dongshan Meixi Du (東山梅溪度禪師語錄), in Meixi Fudu's hall address. Meixi asks whether the assembly's true eye for discerning the teaching is bright and says that if it is, the subtle Way is seen before the eyes and the true source penetrates through the ears.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是正法眼？師云：普。問：如何是端坐念實相？師云：河裏失錢河裏摝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Continued Essentials of Old Recorded Sayings (續古尊宿語要), in Yunmen Wenyan's section, records an unnamed questioner asking, ‘What is the true eye for discerning the teaching?’ Yunmen answers, ‘Universal.’ The unnamed questioner is the exact headword-bearing speaker; Yunmen is the respondent.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 世尊曰。吾有正法眼藏。涅槃妙心。實相無相。微妙法門。不立文字。教外別傳。付囑摩訶迦葉。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Sakyamuni Buddha section: The Buddha utters the longer related compound ‘treasury of the true eye of the teaching’ and entrusts it to Mahakasyapa.
